commitResults.messageBody:
## Summary

Update `delete INDEX` to meet the F4 specification:

* Validate argument count and index format with exact error messages, including oversized integers.
* Delete the selected contact from the currently displayed list while preserving the active filter, remaining order, and other contacts’ information.
* Save a prepared deletion before updating the live model; use atomic file replacement to preserve existing data on save failure.
* Display the required success and empty-list messages, maintain consecutive numbering, and clear input only on success.
* Update user/developer documentation and manual testing instructions.

## Follow-up

Persistent contact-details panel behavior remains with the view-feature owner. The current `view` command displays details in the feedback box.

commitResults.messageTitle: Record undo history for contact changes
commitResults.messageBody:
Contact-changing commands save their results without retaining the
previous contact data.

Undo needs snapshots captured through normal command execution

Introduce UndoableCommand and connect supported commands to session
snapshot storage. Remove session backups during shutdown

Register history only after saving succeeds so failures preserve the
live model, displayed contacts, saved data and existing history

Contact changes retain snapshots, but users cannot restore them through
a command.

Expose history through an argument-free undo command.

Implement UndoCommand using the existing staged-command flow and inject
a narrow UndoHistory dependency through the parser.

Keep undo behavior in the command and persistence orchestration generic.
Consume history only after saving succeeds.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update documentation to record undo behaviour
Add independent contact collections to the model
commitResults.messageBody:
The model holds one address book, and staged commands copy only that
collection.

Favourites need independent data so editing or deleting a contact in one
collection does not affect the other.

Add Contacts and Favourites sections, route model operations to the
active collection, and preserve both in staged commands.

Reuse the existing Model API so contact commands can operate on either
collection without duplicating their logic.

The model supports two collections, but users cannot switch between
them. Startup and command saving still use only the main data file.

Users need to select a collection and manage its contacts without
changing the other collection.

Add the tab command, load favourites at startup, and update the
displayed section, contact list, and save location.

Route both save paths through the selected collection to preserve
save-before-apply guarantees while reusing existing commands.

Users can switch collections but must manually re-enter contacts to add
them to Favourites.

Existing contacts need a direct way to become independent favourites
without losing their details.

Add favourite INDEX with displayed-index validation, duplicate
detection, and a separate error when run from Favourites.

Track the changed collection separately from the active section so
favouriting saves only Favourites while preserving the current Contacts
view and its search filter.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update DG user stories, use cases, and glossary
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide requirements still follow the AB3 sample.
Use cases cover only deleting a person, and the glossary is a table.
User stories also omit several stories from the project direction,
including viewing a person.

Readers cannot tell which contact actions AB4 is meant to support.

Let's,
* fill in the missing user stories and the blank benefit
* add use cases for add, find, view, edit, and adding to a group
* redefine the glossary as a bullet list of AB4 terms

commitResults.messageTitle: Add filter command for contacts by tags
commitResults.messageBody:
find matches any keyword across names, tags, and notes. There is
no way to show only contacts that have every chosen tag.

Let's,
* add filter t/TAG [t/TAG]... with case-insensitive AND matching
* wire FilterCommandParser into AddressBookParser
* cover the command with unit and parser tests
* document filter in the User Guide
* enable assertions for the Gradle run task

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Tab autocomplete for command words
commitResults.messageBody:
The command box requires every command word to be typed in full.
That slows down keyboard use when several commands share a prefix.

Let's,
* add a command-word registry and prefix autocompleter
* complete the first word on Tab and cycle when several match
* leave arguments unchanged and keep Enter execution as-is
* document the behaviour in the User Guide
* cover matching, cycling, and no-match cases with unit tests
